title: FLEET_ONE_JOB_ANTI_JOB_LINT
universal_lens: The fleet lint formalizes a strict partition of the operational Hilbert space. Each seat defines an orthogonal projection operator $P_i$ onto a singular outcome subspace, while anti-jobs and never-lists define the null-space constraints, ensuring the global state evolution remains unitary and free from entangled, fuzzy-vibe cross-talk.
gsi_mapping: In GSI, the one-job rule acts as a hard prior over feature spaces, preventing covariate shift leakage between distinct statistical edges. The never-list functions as a conformal prediction exclusion zone, guaranteeing that out-of-distribution signals do not contaminate the isolated inference manifolds of specific betting markets.
gse_mapping: For GSE, this lint enforces a deterministic finite automaton (DFA) for situational reasoning. State transitions are only permitted within the explicitly defined 'one job' boundary. Escalation to GSE Main represents a meta-stable transition triggered exclusively by unresolvable blocking conditions, maintaining system-wide coherence.

reasoning_traces.retrocausal_genealogy: This primitive traces its lineage to mid-20th century cybernetics and the principles of bounded rationality introduced by Herbert Simon. reasoning_traces.theory_of_mind: From a game-theoretic perspective, this lint models the opposing agents (or internal stakeholders) as rational actors who might otherwise exploit ambiguity to expand their influence or shirk responsibility. By explicitly defining 'anti-jobs', the system pre-empts strategic maneuvering where an agent might claim jurisdiction over a profitable but high-risk area. It assumes that without these hard constraints, agents will naturally drift toward maximizing their own utility at the expense of global coherence. The 'quiet default' further models the cognitive load of the orchestrator, recognizing that constant noise leads to paralysis. Thus, the lint is a defensive architecture against both malicious exploitation and benign cognitive overload, forcing all actors to adhere to a shared, minimal communication protocol.
reasoning_traces.cross_layer_veto: The cross-layer veto condition is triggered when a proposed seat definition exhibits collinearity with existing roles or leaks information across designated security boundaries. Specifically, if the 'one job' statement contains conjunctive operators ('and also'), it fails the orthogonality check, indicating a potential for conflicting gradients during optimization. Similarly, if the 'never-list' does not explicitly gate sensitive data flows (e.g., 'Garrett-facing' or 'tip-sheet copy'), the system vetoes the configuration to prevent epistemic contamination. This veto ensures that the GSI inference layers remain statistically independent, preserving the validity of conformal predictions, while simultaneously guaranteeing that the GSE state machine does not enter undefined or insecure configurations due to overlapping authority matrices.
